From Howard County Office of Emergency Management - Due to the extremely dry conditions in Howard County, a ban on all outdoor burning will be in effect as of today, Aug. 5, and will remain in effect until further notice.

Waste Management asks that all customers follow these guidelines to help ensure timely and safe trash collections:
• Place your trash cart with the wheels facing your house and the lid opening toward the street.
• Keep at least 3 feet of clearance on all sides of each trash cart.
• If you have two trash carts, place them at least 3 feet apart.
• Do not place any trash on top of the carts or on the ground next to them. All trash must be placed inside the cart with the lid completely closed.
Thank you for your cooperation in helping Waste Management provide efficient service to our community.

IMPORTANT NOTICE:
Waste Management has a new trash truck and they are asking to PLEASE leave a 3 foot perimeter around trash cart. If trash cart is up against a mail box it will destory it. Also, new truck will not pick up objects around trash cart. Items need to be inside a trashbag and inside of cart. If you have any questions contact Nashville Water Office at 870-845-1440.

Motorists are advised that Mount Pleasant Drive is closed from Leslie Street to Pope Street until further notice as crews work to install a gas line.

Drivers should plan to use an alternate route and use caution when traveling near the work area. The closure will remain in effect until the project is completed.

Updates will be provided as they become available.
The intersection at S. Jones and Clark Street will be closed beginning Monday, May 11th. It will be closed for at least 10 days or until the work is finished. Thank you for your patience.

City of Nashville spring cleanup week!

April 18th through April 26th

Note to add: NO tires or flammable liquids
City of Nashville offices will be closed on Friday, April 3 in observance of Good Friday. Offices will reopen on Monday, April 6.

With severe weather expected this weekend, we want everyone to be prepared. Please wrap any exposed outdoor pipes and leave cabinet doors open under sinks to allow warm air to circulate.

There is a strong possibility of power outages, so we encourage you to have flashlights, extra batteries, and a safe way to stay warm, as temperatures will be extremely cold. Please remember to bring pets indoors or ensure they have adequate shelter, warmth, food, and water during this time.

We also ask for your patience with our electric crews, who may be working in frigid conditions to restore power as quickly and safely as possible. Likewise, please be patient with City employees as we work to keep everyone safe, clear roads, remove fallen limbs, and ensure water services continue uninterrupted.

Thank you for your understanding and cooperation. Please stay safe.
